speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are suffering from severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria. To begin my assessment, can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and on a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is it?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID). The clinical presentation of severe lower abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dysuria, and dyspareunia in a sexually active 17-year-old female is highly suggestive of PID, likely caused by Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae. I am ready to order a Urinalysis and a Pelvic Ultrasound to confirm the diagnosis and rule out tubo-ovarian abscess.
